title: The Rain's First Touch Meadow

features.name: the first shed
features.desc-on-touch: where farmers kept tools, and still do. the roof reads the rain differently than the open meadow does. you listen to it learning.

features.name: the grass memory
features.desc-on-touch: where rain first touches the meadow, the grass remembers it has always been thirsty. each drop is a small answer that arrives too late.

features.name: the old fence post
features.desc-on-touch: weathered grey, teaching the paddock how to stand still. the rain darkens it and it remembers other storms, earlier seasons.

features.name: the first gathering
features.desc-on-touch: where rain pools at the meadow's low point before it runs downhill. it gathers itself, teaches water what collection means.

features.name: the standing tree
features.desc-on-touch: alone at the meadow's edge, it reads the rain through leaves and roots both. it stands because the water asks it to.

reverie.title: REVERIE — the first rain in the paddock
narr: you both stood in the meadow when the rain began,
neither of you moving toward the shed. the grass grew
dark with water. she tilted her face up and you watched
the rain find her skin. 'it remembers', she said. 'it
always comes back.' you heard it in her voice: she was
teaching the rain, and the rain was listening.

inscription: the creek remembers before it ever learns to forget, and the rain falls as if it has come home
